content.text:
The site matches the approved baselines again at desktop and phone size. Both visual tests pass, and I didn't approve or change any baselines.

Three CSS rules in `site/css/styles.css` had been altered:

- **`.px-lg-5` left padding:** it was `1.5rem` and is now `3rem`. This was the main cause of the layout shift on desktop, because the main containers lost their left padding and the content moved sideways and grew taller.
- **`.navbar-expand-lg .navbar-nav` direction:** it was `column` and is now `row`. The nav links were stacking vertically on desktop.
- **`.form-control` font weight:** it was `700` and is now `400`. The quantity input text had turned bold.

I restored the first two from the pixel diffs and the geometry data. I set the font weight to the standard Bootstrap value, since the page itself doesn't show what the original was. The passing baseline comparison supports all three fixes.
